# skill-forge: what it prints

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_demos.py from real runs; do not edit by
     hand. CI fails when this file no longer matches the code. -->

Real output of [skill-forge](../../plugins/skill-forge) on the fixtures its own
tests use. Skills and subagents are not shown: what they say depends on the
model, and they are measured by the eval cases in the plugin's `evals/`.

## audit_skills.py on three skills with planted faults

A description with no trigger, a bare Bash grant and a name that disagrees with its directory: each loads, and each costs something.

```console
$ python3 plugins/skill-forge/scripts/audit_skills.py plugins/skill-forge/tests/fixtures/broken/no-trigger plugins/skill-forge/tests/fixtures/broken/grant-bare-comma plugins/skill-forge/tests/fixtures/broken/name-mismatch
warn   no-trigger: `description` never says when to use the skill
        It reads as a definition. Add the situation in the words a user would actually type.
warn   no-trigger: `description` opens with "this skill"
        Spend those characters on the trigger instead.
ERROR  grant-bare-comma: `allowed-tools` pre-approves every shell command (Bash)
        The field grants, it does not restrict: whenever the skill fires, any command runs without a prompt. Scope it to the script the skill runs, e.g. Bash(python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check.py *).
warn   name-mismatch: `name` is 'something-else' but the directory is 'name-mismatch'
        The skill loads either way, but the two names do different jobs and they now disagree: in a plugin the command is /<plugin>:something-else, while a personal or project skill is invoked as /name-mismatch and shows 'something-else' in the listing. Match them and the question does not arise.

3 skill(s) audited: 1 error(s), 3 warning(s)
[exit 1]
```
